key_insight: Quantile-based distributional reinforcement learning can estimate return distributions efficiently, with quantile-projected estimators achieving optimal statistical rates and semiparametric efficiency.
engineering_relevance: This provides a principled, sample-efficient way to evaluate policy performance distributionally, which is useful for risk-sensitive decision systems and uncertainty-aware RL pipelines.
method: Build a finite-dimensional return-distribution representation via the quantile-projected Bellman fixed point.
Construct an empirical-MDP estimator under a generative model and derive non-asymptotic $W_\infty$ error bounds.
Prove asymptotic normality, efficiency bounds, and a Berry--Esseen result for smooth functionals.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a non-asymptotic error scaling of $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{m/n})$ and shows the estimator attains the semiparametric efficiency bound in both fixed- and growing-quantile regimes.
watch_item: The strongest guarantees rely on access to a generative model and on smooth functionals, so practical performance may degrade when sampling is limited or the target functional is non-smooth.
paper_title: Statistical Efficiency and Inference of Quantile Distributional Reinforcement Learning
